notes: Summary: Aureus running operator-assist chat for dispatch + high-volume telemetry summarization. Need firm throughput guarantees for peak operations windows.
Customer asks (raw): 'We need predictable throughput — if we pay for reserved capacity we can't have hidden throttles during peak events.'

Throughput negotiation: customer requests a minimum sustained tokens/sec floor of 120000 tokens/sec across the dedicated pool (24/7 baseline) with ability to burst to 480000 tokens/sec for up to 60s, up to 6 times/hour (they provided historical spike traces).

Concurrency caps: want per-model concurrency caps exposed. Proposed: 400 concurrent sessions per model by default; per-tenant hard cap 800. Customer prefers explicit concurrency enforcement vs opaque queueing.

Burst policy: request explicit burst buckets (tokens and seconds); prefer token-bucket style: refill rate tied to baseline reservation, burst allowance resets every hour. Legal wants burst clause in SLA (duration and frequency).

Latency SLOs: target p95 end-to-end response latency < 500ms for 64-token replies at typical prompt lengths (median 48 tokens). Acceptable p99 up to 1.2s for larger summaries. Want traceability to tokens/sec floor if violated.

Reserved GPU planning: customer proposes initial pool = 8x A100/H100 equivalent (region NA), scale plan to 16 GPUs at 6 month mark. Expectation: Redwood to map tokens/sec guarantee to a fixed GPU reservation and provide sizing rationale (profiling data + batch assumptions).
Model preferences: primarily 13B-70B open models (quantized) with a fallback to smaller 7B variant for non-critical ops. Must support kernel selection and quantization recommendations.
Operational asks: prefix/KV cache for session continuity, deterministic autoscaling triggers, per-route throttles, and ability to pin model versions for rollouts.

Security/compliance: VPC/private control plane required for EU operations; KMS/HSM integration mandatory; SOC2 evidence requested before procurement; audit log retention requirement = 3 years (stated).
Cost sensitivity: willing to commit to annual reserved capacity if unit economics are guaranteed; asking for graduated credits if throughput/latency SLOs not met (not just uptime credits).

POC plan: 2-week soak with instrumented traffic generator using their sequence distribution (Diego to provide benchmark harness). Success metrics: sustained >=120k tokens/sec baseline, p95 latency target met, no unexpected queueing beyond agreed concurrency caps.
Open items for legal: SLA credit calculation when degraded tokens/sec vs. uptime; force majeure definitions for cloud provider outages; burst overage pricing model.
Customer quote in meeting: 'We can't have surprises in throughput during service disruptions — we need contractual guarantees that map to hardware.'

Internal: SE will run profiling on representative models (13B/70B) with their prompt set; ask infra to pre-validate H100 capacity in target region; finance to draft ARR estimate with commitment tiers.
